title: Representation theorem
statement: OC-M adequacy roles represent the required surfaces of observable/articulable system descriptions.
formal_proposition: For any MetaLanguage L, if Adequate L then L has each AdequacyRole: observation coverage, distinguishability, dynamics, pressure, repair, extension, collapse, underdetermination, projection non-inflation, evidence binding, and compositional refinement.
assumptions: Observable/articulable reality is modeled as descriptions satisfying the adequacy-role index; no claim is made about unarticulated facts without observation binding.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean representation_theorem proves the role coverage statement directly from Adequate L.
falsifier_check: A counterexample would be an Adequate L lacking an AdequacyRole; this contradicts the Adequate definition and is covered by removing_any_adequacy_role_breaks_adequacy.
dependency_closure: Depends on formal AdequacyRole and Adequate definitions.

title: Necessity theorem
statement: Any adequate metamodel contains every OC-M adequacy role.
formal_proposition: For all L, Adequate L implies every r : AdequacyRole is present in L.
assumptions: Adequacy axioms define the target class of universal metaontologies; outside that class the theorem does not apply.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean theorem representation_theorem and removing_any_adequacy_role_breaks_adequacy establish necessity and lower-bound failure.
falsifier_check: A rival missing observation, dynamics, pressure, repair, extension, collapse, underdetermination, projection discipline, evidence, or refinement fails the missing-role witness.
independent_verification: Python minimality_witnesses.py removes each role and confirms inadequacy.

title: Uniqueness up to definitional equivalence
statement: Every adequate metamodel is definitionally equivalent to OC-M on the required adequacy-role profile.
formal_proposition: RoleEquivalent OCMeta L holds for any Adequate L over the AdequacyRole index.
assumptions: Equivalence is over required adequacy roles. Extra structure is a non-minimal extension unless it solves a distinct formal obligation.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean minimal_uniqueness_up_to_definitional_equivalence proves bidirectional role equivalence over the adequacy-role index.
falsifier_check: A counterexample must be adequate while lacking a required role; that is impossible by Adequate L.
dependency_closure: Depends on OCMeta, RoleEquivalent, and Adequate.
independent_verification: lake build verifies the theorem; validator enforces article wording.

title: No eliminable primitive
statement: Removing any OC-M adequacy role breaks adequacy.
formal_proposition: For every missing role r, missingRoleLanguage r is not Adequate.
assumptions: Roles are typed adequacy obligations, not merely names.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean removing_any_adequacy_role_breaks_adequacy proves the universal removal theorem.
falsifier_check: A falsifier would show missingRoleLanguage r is adequate for some r; Lean reduces this to r != r.
dependency_closure: Depends on AdequacyRole decidable equality and Adequate.
independent_verification: Python witness enumerates all role removals.

title: Operator minimality under typed effects
statement: The six continuum operators are minimal under typed semantic effect signatures.
formal_proposition: OperatorAdequate L requires introduce, differentiate, stabilize, project, invalidate, and repair. Removing any one operator role breaks OperatorAdequate L; operatorCode is injective.
assumptions: The theorem is relative to typed semantic effects. A generic rewrite operator is not a role-preserving replacement.
falsifier_check: A falsifier must remove an operator role while preserving all typed effects; Python and Lean removal witnesses reject this.
dependency_closure: Depends on OperatorRole, OperatorAdequate, and typed role signatures.

title: Central principle repaired theorem
statement: The central principle is the four-outcome stress-response taxonomy, not the old two-outcome fork.
formal_proposition: For every StressContext, classify returns absorption, extension, collapse, or underdetermined.
assumptions: Structured pressure must declare evidenceBound, sameDescriptionRepair, extensionRepair, and invariantFailure.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean central_four_outcome_taxonomy proves exhaustiveness; absorption_is_counterexample_to_old_two_fork preserves the guard against the old fork.
falsifier_check: A same-description repair case is a counterexample to the old fork but not to OC-M.
dependency_closure: Depends on 027/028 repair and standalone 029 StressContext.
independent_verification: lake build verifies the taxonomy theorem.

title: Parametric K-ladder theorem
statement: K-levels are derived as a parametric closure/rank ladder with adjacent non-collapse.
formal_proposition: kRank n < kRank (n+1) for every n; kLadder maxDepth is List.range (maxDepth + 1).
assumptions: The proof derives ladder form from a rank/closure parameter; it does not smuggle in a cosmic fixed count.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean k_adjacent_noncollapse and k_ladder_reference_13_count prove adjacent rank growth and the reference depth-12 count.
falsifier_check: A falsifier would need adjacent ranks n and n+1 to collapse under kRank n = n; Nat.lt_succ_self rules this out.
dependency_closure: Depends on Nat rank rule and parameterized kLadder.

title: Old absolute K0-K12 uniqueness refuted and repaired
statement: Absolute non-parametric K0-K12 uniqueness is not derivable from the minimal metaontology.
formal_proposition: There exists an alternative depth whose kLadder length is not 13; therefore exact count 13 is not absolute without a depth parameter.
assumptions: K0-K12 survives as a reference instantiation at maxDepth 12, not as a theorem that reality has exactly 13 possible levels.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean fixed_k_count_not_absolute constructs alternativeDepth 13 with length 14; Python checks len(k_ladder(13)) != 13.
falsifier_check: This refutes only absolute count wording, not the parametric K-ladder theorem.
dependency_closure: Depends on OC29-T007 and 028 K repair guard.
independent_verification: lake build and Python witness both check the repair.

title: Law admissibility theorem
statement: Law-like OC statements are admissible only with trigger, scope, outcome criterion, and falsifier.
formal_proposition: LawAdmissible L entails L.falsifier and includes trigger, scope, and outcomeCriterion.
assumptions: Unconditional law slogans are outside article-eligible theorem language.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean law_admissibility_requires_falsifier proves the key non-rhetorical gate.
falsifier_check: A law without falsifier cannot satisfy LawAdmissible.
independent_verification: Validator enforces article boundary against unconditional wording.

title: Crown stones rejected from core alone
statement: Crown stones are not core theorems from the minimal metaontology alone.
formal_proposition: coreOnlyDomainClaim has coreSignature True but localInstantiation and evidenceBound False; CrownPromoted coreOnlyDomainClaim is false.
assumptions: A crown stone can be promoted later only by its own theorem chain or domain evidence.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean crown_not_core_from_signature_only proves core signature alone cannot promote a crown claim.
falsifier_check: A falsifier would validate a crown from core signature without local instantiation; Lean coreOnlyDomainClaim blocks it.
independent_verification: Article boundary forbids crown promotion from core alone.

title: Domain projection theorem
statement: Domain projections require local instantiation and evidence.
formal_proposition: DomainValidated D entails localInstantiation and evidenceBound.
assumptions: OC-M is a metaontology, not automatic empirical validation.
proof_or_counterproof: Lean domain_projection_non_inflation and core_signature_alone_cannot_validate_domain prove the domain gate.
falsifier_check: A falsifier would validate a domain with coreSignature alone and no local evidence; Lean blocks it.
dependency_closure: Depends on projection non-inflation inherited from 027/028 and restated in 029.

title: Article boundary theorem binding
statement: Article boundary follows the 029 proof ledger and blocks overclaim reintroduction.
formal_proposition: The article may claim minimal universal metaontology only up to definitional equivalence under adequacy axioms; it must not promote old fork, absolute K count, crown/domain proof without evidence, or unqualified alternatives-worse wording.
assumptions: Article language is part of the proof boundary, not a proof substitute.
proof_or_counterproof: validate_029.py checks DB completeness, artifact existence, allowed statuses, and boundary hygiene.
falsifier_check: A promoted forbidden phrase fails validation.
dependency_closure: Depends on all 029 proof rows and article boundary file.
